conflicts.stem: Blizzards are characteristic of
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'Temperate region'. Blizzards occur in both polar regions and high-latitude temperate interiors; the stored key (Antarctic) is kept.

conflicts.stem: Plains formed due to the filling up of lakes are called
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'karst plains', which form by limestone solution, not lake filling. The precise term is lacustrine plains; stored key 'alluvial' kept.

conflicts.stem: INS Beas, the guided missile frigate was commissioned in
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys Mumbai. Stored key Kolkata kept; INS Beas was built at GRSE Kolkata and commissioned there on 11 July 2005 per Navy records as recalled - not independently verified here.

conflicts.stem: In Andhra Pradesh as on July, 2008 the hamlet which has achieved 100 percent literacy is
conflicts.note: Key is a third-party compilation (status unknown); the draft wrongly keyed Atmakur; the stored key (Sovva) is followed. Not independently verified.

conflicts.stem: In 1932 a committee was appointed, under the Chairmanship of Aravamudu Iyengar by the Nizam of Hyderabad. It was mainly to suggest measures for
conflicts.note: The stem's '1932' is wrong: the committee was appointed in 1937 (report 1938). Purpose (key) is correct.

conflicts.stem: Who of the following was the first Secretary of the Andhra unit of the Socialist Party ?
conflicts.note: App notes give N.G. Ranga as president and Madduri Annapurnayya as secretary (June 1934); key (Ranga as secretary) kept.

conflicts.stem: Ryotwari system was first introduced in the Madras Presidency in
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys option 1 (Rayalaseema). Stored key Baramahals is correct for 'Madras Presidency' (Read & Munro, 1792); Rayalaseema is right only for 'first in Andhra'. Key kept.

conflicts.stem: Who of the following rulers built Rajahmundry ?
conflicts.note: Conflict: app notes (and several PYQ keys) credit Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI, title Rajamahendra), which is option 2 here. Key (Rajaraja Narendra) kept.

conflicts.stem: During the Vandemataram Movement, Bipinchandra Pal visited Andhra districts. When he was in Machilipatnam, he was the guest of
conflicts.note: Conflict: app notes (Swadeshi in Andhra) give Ramadasu Naidu (option 1) as Pal's host and list Kopalle as a disputed key. Key kept.

conflicts.stem: The transaction demand for money, according to W.J. Baumol, depends on
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'rate of interest and supply of money'; Baumol's model gives income and interest. Stored key kept – it is correct.

conflicts.stem: Which State in India has the largest number of towns ?
conflicts.note: POSSIBLE CONFLICT: Census 2011 gives Tamil Nadu the most towns (1,097 vs UP 915); UP leads only in statutory towns. Key (UP) kept as printed; treat with caution.

conflicts.stem: India's industrial policy in respect of foreign multinationals in recent years has been
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'making their ownership more in India' (the FERA-era policy). Post-1991 policy is encouragement. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: The Reserve Bank of India issues all currency notes except
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'Rs 500'; that is wrong – RBI issues Rs 500 notes. Stored key (Re 1) kept.

conflicts.stem: What is trade point ?
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'centrally controlled stock market'; UNCTAD defines Trade Points as networked trade-facilitation centres. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: The first 20-Point Programme was announced by Smt. Indira Gandhi in
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 1974; the programme was announced 1 July 1975. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: A hypothesis is tested by
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'realism of its assumptions' – the position Friedman rejects. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: The idea of balanced growth is related to the classical
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'full employment equilibrium'; Nurkse explicitly ties it to Say's law. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: Assume that an ad valorem tax is imposed on a commodity. The price of that commodity will rise if its elasticity of demand is
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'more than unity'; incidence theory supports zero. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: Which one of the following is the largest source of 'net invisible' in India's foreign trade on current account ?
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'tourism'; RBI data show remittances largest. Stored key kept. (Remittances are themselves private transfers – option 3 overlaps.)

conflicts.stem: Autarky is a state of
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'no trade because there is no gain at all from trade' – that adds a false reason. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: Rising prices and inflation in India have
conflicts.note: CONFLICT: a third-party compilation keys 'adverse effect on investment' alone; all three effects are standard. Stored key kept.

conflicts.stem: Bats move during night time with the help of
conflicts.note: Ultrasound is itself sound; 'Sound waves' is wrong only in the sense of audible sound, and 'ultrasonic rays' is loose wording. Key kept.

conflicts.stem: Surya Siddhanta was written by
conflicts.note: Conflict: Surya Siddhanta has no known author (often ascribed to Maya; summarised by Varahamihira); many GK sources credit Aryabhata, as the key does. 'None of the above' is arguably correct. Key retained.

conflicts.stem: The variety of Iron ore with the highest quality is
conflicts.note: Conflict: NCERT X says 'Magnetite is the finest iron ore with a very high content of iron up to 70%'; hematite is 'the most important industrial iron ore'. Key (Hematite) retained.

conflicts.stem: Identity below the cause of the dispute between mill owners and workers, which led to the mill workers strike in 1917 at Ahmedabad.
conflicts.note: Dispute arose in 1917 but the strike and Gandhi's fast were in Feb–Mar 1918; the stem's '1917' refers to the dispute. Key kept.

conflicts.stem: The third phase of agricultural development in India is characterized by
conflicts.note: App notes (3:57:5) list price-support (MSP/procurement) as the 'third phase'; textbook periodisations differ. APPSC final key (option 4) kept.

conflicts.stem: Which of the following country is the largest producer of pearls?
conflicts.note: Conflict: by current volume China (freshwater pearls) is the largest producer; key (Japan) retained.

conflicts.stem: "Right to life" does not include "right to die". It has been held in case of
conflicts.key: Chenna Jagadeswar v. State of A.P.
conflicts.note: Key kept. The draft analysis wrongly keyed Gian Kaur; APPSC's key is Chenna Jagadeeswar (AP HC 1988), which held the same.

conflicts.stem: The Chalukya King who is said to have built 108 Saiva temples was:
conflicts.note: Conflict: app notes credit Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja); key kept.

conflicts.stem:

i. Under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act (RPA) 1951, no election can be called in question except by an election petition presen
conflicts.note: 'Only the High Courts' is true for RPA elections; Presidential/VP election disputes are decided by the Supreme Court (Art 71).

conflicts.stem:

Reason (R) : The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) made changes to the Preamble, the Seventh Schedu

conflicts.note: Conflict: Charlotte Edwards (England, 2,605 T20I runs, retired 2016) crossed 2000 T20I runs before Mithali Raj; Mithali was the first Indian (ICC/Cricinfo records). Key kept.
